reasons: Both answers identify the shared dual-write problem, reject publishing before commit because it produces phantom orders, propose one shared outbox with at-least-once delivery and idempotent consumers, and apply it to each case with case-specific details (TTL as a backstop, versioning or double delete, and email dedup in a worker). A gives slightly more diagnostic depth (mandatory/durability checks, early consumer visibility, a DEL-before-commit check). B adds a useful AFTER_COMMIT+@Async trade-off and the concrete Spring config keys, so neither is clearly better.
